beats.care: Your last-mile ride from the Metro may get less crowded, but possibly harder to find at peak hours.
beats.what: The Transport Department's draft caps Delhi at 2.5 lakh e-rickshaws, with four passengers each and a 25 km/h limit.
beats.why: Officials point to jams near markets and Metro stations, road safety and pollution.

cards.body: No new registrations beyond this unless the cap is revised. The rules are not in force yet.
cards.caption: most e-rickshaws Delhi would register

cards.body: Drivers need a licence and PSV badge. Each vehicle needs a digital compliance certificate valid for two years. No disturbing music. Unregistered e-rickshaws can be impounded and crushed.
cards.title: Other rules in the draft

opts: A draft open for public suggestions
cards.q: What is the status of these e-rickshaw rules right now?
cards.why: It is a draft scheme; the public has 30 days to send suggestions.

hook: Could your e-rickshaw ride *soon have only four seats*?

learn.t: Under the draft, nobody may sit beside the e-rickshaw driver, and top speed is capped at 25 km/h.
